text: "Where there is no vision (chazon), the people perish." Before God does anything, He gives a vision.
explanation:
In Samuel's childhood, "the word of the Lord was rare in those days; there was no widespread revelation." The word for vision there, chazon, is the same one in Proverbs: "Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint." People don't perish for lack of money or connections, but for lack of a God-given picture of the future.

That's why the enemy works so hard to fill your mind with dark images. He robs your vision before he robs you. But God is restoring hope to His people: a confident expectation of good. Ask Him for His vision for your family, your health and your work, and let it shape how you face each day.

text: "The word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision: 'I am your shield.'" Abram answered, "Seeing I go childless…"
explanation:
God's word came to Abram as a picture: a shield, and an exceedingly great reward. But Abram's inner picture hadn't changed: "Lord God, what will You give me, seeing I go childless?" So God took him outside and said, "Look now toward heaven, and count the stars… So shall your descendants be." Night after night, the stars filled his heart with a new picture. "And he believed in the Lord."

God often has to change the vision inside before the outside changes. What do you see when you think of your future: "Seeing I've been retrenched… seeing the doctor said…"? Let God replace that picture with His.

text: "Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks." Change the pictures in your heart, and your words will follow.
explanation:
"A good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings forth good." We often focus on making our mouths say the right things, but if our hearts still hold images of fear, the words feel hollow and we feel like hypocrites. The mouth only overflows with what fills the heart.

That's why God speaks in pictures: a tree by rivers of water whose leaf doesn't wither, a shield, a land as far as you can see. Fill your heart with what God shows you. "Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it spring the issues of life." Guard what you let in, and good things will come out.

text: "What God has cleansed you must not call common." Stop labelling people. Every one of them is someone Christ died for.
explanation:
On a Joppa rooftop at noon, Peter saw a sheet full of animals that were unclean under the law, and heard, "Rise, Peter; kill and eat." When he refused, the voice said, "What God has cleansed you must not call common." It happened three times. Then messengers from a Gentile centurion arrived, and Peter understood: "God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean."

We're quick to put people into categories and dismiss whole groups. But in God's eyes there's one category of people outside Christ: sinners He loves. Laws and labels never change a heart; the gospel does. Fellowship with believers, yes, but don't keep your distance from those who need Jesus.

text: "That the eyes of your heart may be enlightened." The Spirit of wisdom works by flooding your heart's eyes with light.
explanation:
Paul prays for believers who already have the Holy Spirit, that God "may give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him, the eyes of your understanding being enlightened." The heart has eyes. The word enlightened, photizo (as in photo), means flooded with light.

When God filled Bezalel "with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding," he could design the ark and the golden lampstand. That's how wisdom feels: "I see it! Now I know what to do." Pray this prayer daily over yourself and your children, and expect to see what others miss: in your work, your parenting and your walk with God.

text: Cornelius wasn't saved yet, but his prayers rose "for a memorial before God." God always finds the one reaching for Him.
explanation:
Cornelius was a Roman soldier who gave generously and prayed to God always, though he hadn't yet heard the gospel. An angel told him, "Your prayers and your alms have come up for a memorial before God," and sent him to find Peter, "who will tell you words by which you and all your household will be saved." He gathered his relatives and close friends to hear, and while Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on them all.

People ask, "What about those who never hear about Jesus?" Cornelius is the answer: if a heart cries out for God, God will send the word. And you can be like him, inviting family and friends to hear.

text: Scripture speaks of "the evil day" (singular) and "good days" (plural).
explanation:
"Take up the whole armour of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day." Day, singular. But "he who would love life and see good days": plural. Hard seasons come, but they're brief compared to the good ones God has planned.

It's scriptural to expect good days. Elihu, who spoke for God in the book of Job, said that those who hear and serve Him "shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures." Don't let anyone talk you out of expecting a year with many beautiful days.
